accuracy.evidence: The four-part model is Rosenberg's Nonviolent Communication (observation, feeling, need, request), including his point that 'I feel that you…' expresses a thought, not a feeling; checked against Rosenberg (2015, 3rd ed.). Apology components (name the act, take responsibility, acknowledge impact, commit to change; no 'but', no 'if') match Lewicki, Polin and Lount (2016) on effective apologies. Curriculum claims checked against DfE RSE statutory guidance 2019 (secondary: healthy friendships, trust, managing conflict) and the PSHE Association KS3 programme. The friendship research claim is kept modest ('suggest… goes with') per Laursen, Finkelstein and Betts (2001) meta-analysis of peer conflict resolution. The trust chart (+10 per kept week, -25 per slip) is labelled as a model, not data. Parameterised items checked at corners: p2 t+10w 30..90, p4 t-25 15..65, m5 s+kw 20..90, m9 m-r 2..9.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the real errors teenagers make: 'always/never' framing (OBSWHY for 'You always ignore me', NVCWHY always, m7), labels and name-calling (label), 'I feel that…' pseudo-feelings (step 2 prediction, CQ feelword, m2), dragging in 'everyone says' (gossip), vague or ordering requests (vague, demand, CQ polite/order, p5), the if-pology and 'but' (step 3 prediction, CQ word, p3), minimising with 'only joking' (joke), expecting trust to return at once (step 4 prediction, CQ louder/gift, m4), and avoidance as a fix (step 5 prediction, CQ vanish/strong, m6).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagrepair models this topic's own mechanisms: fact-vs-judgement sorting, a four-slot NVC builder where each slot cycles through one clean and two specific failure options, an apology builder whose repair meter is cancelled by blame lines, an 8-week trust chart with asymmetric gain and loss, and a 10-week avoid-vs-talk comparison. flagagree (7-9) cools a cross-o-meter and finds a fair fix; flagsorry (4-5) matches fix-its to hurts; neither has NVC parts, a repair meter or trust over time. Max 6-shingle similarity 6.7% (flag_chunk.js).

lab_teaches.evidence: Each idea is found before it is stated: each wrong card or option gets its own explanation and the 'how it lands' meter moves from 'they will defend' to 'they can hear you' as parts get clean; adding 'Sorry if you were upset' or '…but you overreact' visibly drops the repair meter even with good lines present; the trust bars climb 10 points per kept week and fall 25 on a slip, so the learner feels the asymmetry; the avoid line slides down while the talk line dips and then rises above it.

predictions.evidence: Five predictions, each with a tempting wrong option disproved: 'You always ignore me' as an observation, 'I felt that you are a liar' as a feeling, the if-and-but apology as real, trust returning 'straight away', and friends ending 'further apart' after a well-handled falling-out.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Twelve distinct slip messages in slip(): label, gossip, word, short, feelword, honest, louder, gift, vanish, strong, polite, order. The builders add per-option feedback (nine NVCWHY entries, seven SAYWHY entries) and the sorting step explains every card (OBSWHY), so no wrong choice gets a generic 'try again'.

readability.evidence: validate_lessons passes for the learner audience: kid FK 5.1, adult FK 9.4 (rewritten from 12.4 on the first check). Terms (observation, judgement, request) are defined in plain words on first use with an example. Canvas text wraps onto cards at 13-16 px bold dark ink on pale cards, so long sentences never shrink to fit.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate passes (no banned phrases; explanation overlap 0.2% at most). Kid paragraphs: judgement vs observation; feeling, need and request with the 'I feel that' trap; real vs face-saving apology; trust over time and avoidance. Adult paragraphs: curriculum and key words; sources; named mistakes; what the lab does and its limit (bullying and abuse need an adult).

mobile.evidence: Screenshots after Show me on every step at 360 px Android (light), iPhone 13 (dark) and desktop (dark). A taller phone canvas (1.3) fits the four NVC rows and four apology lines without clipping; text wraps rather than shrinking. Added axis labels (Full trust, Week 1/8, How close you are, Week 1/10) after the first pass showed unlabelled charts. Apology tray buttons wrap their long text across the full width.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button ('This card is a judgement', 'Try the next feeling option', 'Add the line …' / 'Remove the line …', 'This week, keep your word', 'Have the honest talk and see what happens'). tell() updates the canvas aria-label and narration with the full text of each choice. walk.cjs: desktop and iPhone 13 complete all 5 tasks with Show me, the challenge shows, axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in both themes, no console errors.
